title: Request Inkpot — raw synthesis & mini-experiments
body:
Purpose:
This is a working synthesis of ~18 customer threads (support + AE calls) about runtime friction, ambiguous cost signals, and small feature asks. Intended to be compact: raw quotes, quick themes, and a prioritized set of low-risk mini-experiments we can kick off in the next 6 weeks. Not polished — notes to self and to eng/product partners.

Collection method:
- Pulled raw threads from CS inbox (Mar 5–Mar 25), two Zoom calls with customers X and Y (recordings linked in Slack), and AE summaries.
- Quick triage: mark as (P1-P3) where P1 = blocking customer adoption, P2 = recurring annoyance with clear pattern, P3 = one-offs or exploratory asks.

Representative raw snippets (verbatim-ish):
- "Our chat tool suddenly costs 4x after the change — need per-route cost alarms or at least a way to cap token spend per API key." — startup integrating chat flows (P1)
- "KV cache behaviour is opaque. Sometimes responses get stale for a few hours and it's killing our UX. We need explicit cache invalidation or TTL control per customer." — enterprise knowledge base (P2)
- "When we fail over to cheaper model variant, request latency spikes. We want a transparent reroute that keeps latency under SLOs." — marketplace app (P2)
- "Embeddings drifted between model versions; we need a way to pin version+quantization pair and get deterministic embeddings back." — search/product analytics (P2)
- "Can we surface trace id in the streaming payload? Our tracing depends on it for correlating UX traces." — observability-focused customer (P3)

Quick themes (synthesized):
1) Cost visibility & per-route controls — customers want early warnings (alerts/thresholds), soft caps, and per-key quotas. Many are hesitant to trust global billing dashboards.
2) KV cache control & staleness — recurring requests to make cache TTLs and invalidation explicit and per-customer or per-route. Several workarounds in field are fragile (manual bumping, cold-starts).
3) Graceful fallback ergonomics — model variant fallback works but has latency/quality regressions; customers want a predictable low-latency slowpath or transparent stepping stones.
4) Inference determinism (embeddings/versioning) — pinned variant configuration and a compatibility guarantee for embeddings APIs (or automatic migration helpers).
5) Observability hooks for user-level tracing — small ask but high value to reduce debug time (expose trace_id in streaming messages, per-request metadata).

Hypothesis / customer impact scoring (1-5 scale):
- Cost controls: impact 5, frequency 5, effort (engineering rough) 3 — will convert more mid-market customers to self-serve.
- KV cache control: impact 4, frequency 4, effort 3 — reduces support churn/false-positive complaints.
- Fallback ergonomics: impact 4, frequency 3, effort 4 — improves reliability story for PLG customers with spikes.
- Embedding pinning: impact 3, frequency 3, effort 4 — important for search-heavy customers but narrower audience.
- Tracing hooks: impact 2, frequency 4, effort 1 — quick developer UX wins, supports observability sales plays.

Proposed mini-experiments (ranked: cheap -> medium -> heavier):
A) Cheap (1–2 week dev) — "trace-bag": include optional header X-Redwood-Trace in streaming chunks and surface it in Console logs (CS + SRE experiment). Expected impact: fast debug wins. Owner: Riley. Jira: CS-9877.

B) Cheap (2 week dev) — "soft-quota": add per-API-key soft quota with webhooks on threshold (75%, 90%, 100%) and a runtime flag to reject or allow with warning. Low-risk UI and backend change. Owner: Miguel. Jira: CS-9881.

C) Medium (3–4 week) — "kv-ttl-hook": expose per-route KV cache TTL and an admin endpoint to invalidate prefixes (authz guarded). Add telemetry for stale-hit rates. Expected reduction in support tickets for KB customers. Owner: Eng-serving-runtime (TBD). Jira: CS-9890.

D) Medium (4–6 week) — "fallback-slowpath": implement a small low-latency fallback path using a cached short-context model; expose a routing policy config (latency ceiling + quality floor). This smooths failovers. Owner: Serving-runtime. Jira: CS-9897.

E) Heavier (8+ weeks) — "embed-pin": support model-version+quantization pinning and a migration tool that recomputes embeddings with notice. Owner: Product-optimize + Applied-ML. Jira: CS-9905.

Engineering notes / implementation constraints (raw):
- KV TTL needs careful interaction with prefix-based memoization and prefix-sharing across customers — may require namespacing on storage layer.
- Soft-quota: opt for webhook first; hard-reject later if customers want.
- Trace header should be optional; avoid PII leakage. Add sampling to avoid log noise.
- Fallback-slowpath: can initially route to existing small models (open-source) in the model-catalog; later we can support lighter compiled kernels.

Suggested immediate actions (next 2 weeks):
1) Kick off A) trace-bag as a low-effort experiment: Riley + SRE to implement and CS to surface to 3 pilot customers. Goal: 2 customers onboarded, measure reduction in avg debug time.
2) Start design for B) soft-quota: product + billing + console to spec the thresholds and webhook payload. Quick mock in the Console by end of sprint.
3) Align Eng-serving-runtime on C) kv-ttl-hook: 30-min sync; draft scope and identify storage owner.
4) Create a compact customer-facing one-pager that explains fallback semantics and options (helps sales + AE conversations). Owner: Tanya.

Open questions / risks (unsorted):
- Pricing interplay: If we add per-route caps, how do we reflect bumped/blocked requests in invoices? Need finance + billing input.
- Security: cache invalidation endpoints create a potential vector for accidental mass invalidations — auth + rate limits required.
- Expectations: embedding pinning promises determinism. Need to define compatibility windows and deprecation policy.

Notes to CS reps (how to frame to customers):
- Empathize with cost/latency pain; propose short-term workarounds (manual alerts + usage reviews) while offering to enroll them in pilot for soft-quota and trace-bag.
- For embedding customers: offer to run a migration job as a managed service while we build pinning support.

Appendix: quick raw thread map (id -> short):
- thread-3421: startup-chat-cost-spike — P1 — asked for immediate cap
- thread-3489: enterprise-kv-staleness — P2 — KB customer with repeated stale answers
- thread-3540: marketplace-fallback-latency — P2 — wants transparent stepping
- call-03-11: demo + asks from search-customer (embedding pin request)

Internal seed links (copy to product notes):
- Confluence design stub: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/Inkpot+-+Design-Stub
- Slack thread with raw excerpts: slack://channel?team=redwood&channel=cs-runtime-inkpot

Questions for product:
- Will we treat soft quota as a feature gated by paid tier or make it widely available?
- What SLOs do we commit to for fallback-slowpath?

Small to-do list (me / CS):
- Aisha: draft pilot email and onboard 3 customers to trace-bag by Apr 7.
- Miguel: prototype webhook payload and mock Console flow by Apr 12.
- Riley: small PR for trace header in streaming path (instrumentation + docs).
- Tanya: 1-pager for sales/AE by Apr 10.

Closing:
This is intentionally a messy capture — goal is to catalyze fast, measurable experiments that reduce support load and make the platform feel safer for customers experimenting with higher volume. If approved, product + serving-runtime can pick the first two and we’ll run a 6-week learning loop.

-- end of notes --
